sources.evidence_limit: FOR jumps are a deliberate Pythonic extension; scope cleanup, statuses and finite pipe snapshots are offline contracts, not native scheduling or controller equivalence

for_jumps.transfers: Labels and jumps within active FOR scopes retain their captured bounds and iteration state; exiting scopes clear their counters before target execution
for_jumps.guards: No entry into unstarted FOR or uncaptured USING scopes, cross-body jumps, active-counter writes or nested counter reuse
for_jumps.lifetime: Preserve normal and DOWNTO iteration, bound evaluation order, pause/resume and cleanup on RETURN, ABORT, runtime error, budget exhaustion and stop

scoped_group_locks.configuration: Additional callee_scopes flag defaults false and requires apply_directives=true; both true flags persist, ownership and live scope frames do not
scoped_group_locks.entry: Defining source module policy at called-program/internal-routine/FROM-definition entry; atomically acquire additional groups under the stable caller root
scoped_group_locks.cleanup: Release only eligible additional grants owned by the scope; retain caller groups, recursive grants, manual unlock/reacquisition and foreign owners; pause retains scope
scoped_group_locks.boundary: No inferred bank, native wait, physical motion or servo ownership; legacy root-only mode remains available

pipe_wildcards.selection: Bounded configured plain pipe COPY/DELETE batches, with finite retained-byte snapshots and portable destination templates; no real IPC or producer waiting
pipe_wildcards.publication: Preflight complete source/target aliases, busy/pending state, configuration, capacity and ordinary backend quotas before mutation; no circular truncation or implicit configuration
pipe_wildcards.boundary: Socket/DAQ routes and wildcard RENAME remain unavailable; rooted host publication retains its explicit per-file partial-failure boundary

historical_notes: Supersedes blanket FOR-body jump, callee directive-scope and plain PIP wildcard exclusions; historical per-feature ledger versions and internal strict restrictions remain preserved.
